identity.title: On the Role of Attention Heads in Large Language Model Safety

problem.claim: The paper investigates how standard multi-head attention mechanisms relate to LLM safety capability.

gap.claim: Existing safety-mechanism research tends to overlook the safety impact of multi-head attention in mechanistic interpretability.

contributions.claim: Introduces Safety Head ImPortant Score (Ships) to assess individual attention heads’ contributions to model safety.
Generalizes Ships to the dataset level and introduces Sahara to attribute critical safety attention heads inside a model.
Reports that specific attention heads substantially affect safety and primarily function as safety feature extractors.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present their attribution approach and findings as a novel perspective for unpacking safety mechanisms in large models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ablating one safety head in an aligned model such as Llama-2-7b-chat enabled responses to 16× more harmful queries while modifying 0.006% of parameters, compared with approximately 5% in previous studies.
The authors report comprehensive experiments indicating that models fine-tuned from the same base model exhibit overlapping safety heads.
The authors report that special attention heads have a significant impact on safety.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM safety guardrails can be circumvented, and suppressing safety representations or components compromises safety capability.
The paper identifies insufficient attention to multi-head attention’s safety impact.
It proposes Ships and extends it into dataset-level attribution through Sahara.
Reported findings link specific heads to safety, including strong single-head ablation effects and overlap across models sharing a base model.
The approach and findings are framed as a perspective for interpreting black-box safety mechanisms.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a component-level metric with a dataset-level attribution algorithm, then reports both localized ablation effects and cross-model head overlap.

lessons.interpretation: Aligning an attribution method with targeted intervention and transfer-pattern analysis can make a mechanistic claim more concrete.
lessons.application: For a component-analysis paper, pair importance scoring with a localized intervention and a comparison across related model variants.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when interventions are unsafe, prohibitively costly, or the component decomposition is not stable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify Ships or Sahara’s computation, datasets, baselines, or evaluation protocol.
The reported 16× effect is tied to an example aligned model; broader model and task scope is unspecified.
The abstract does not provide details needed to assess the reported experiments or the meaning of “primarily” as feature extractors.
